title: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats

nodes.title: 1. **Use Strong, Unique Passwords**
nodes.summary: Create complex passwords with a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols; avoid reusing the same password across sites, and use a trusted password manager to store credentials.

nodes.title: 2. **Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)**
nodes.summary: Add a second layer of security by enabling 2FA on all important accounts, including email, banking, and social media.

nodes.title: 3. **Beware of Phishing Scams**
nodes.summary: Avoid clicking suspicious links or downloading unknown attachments; verify email addresses and URLs, and never share personal information over email or phone unless you initiated the contact.

nodes.title: 4. **Keep Software Up to Date**
nodes.summary: Regularly update your operating system, apps, browsers, and antivirus programs to patch known vulnerabilities.

nodes.title: 5. **Secure Your Devices**
nodes.summary: Use a screen lock (PIN, password, or fingerprint) on smartphones and computers, and install trusted antivirus and anti-malware software.

nodes.title: 6. **Use Secure Connections**
nodes.summary: Avoid public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions and use a VPN when needed; only enter personal or financial information on HTTPS websites.

nodes.title: 7. **Monitor Bank and Credit Accounts**
nodes.summary: Review statements regularly for unauthorized transactions and set up instant alerts for account activity.

nodes.title: 8. **Manage Privacy Settings**
nodes.summary: Limit personal information shared on social media, adjust privacy controls, and be wary of apps requesting unnecessary permissions.

nodes.title: 9. **Backup Important Data**
nodes.summary: Regularly back up your files to a secure cloud service or external device to protect against data loss.

nodes.title: 10. **Educate Yourself & Stay Informed**
nodes.summary: Learn about new and emerging online threats and participate in cybersecurity awareness programs to stay alert and proactive.
